answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by charging every identity rent in verifiable work each epoch. To stay active, an agent must submit a fresh proof that it completed a useful job, bound to its own key and the current epoch number: timber cut for one jetty cannot be reused to build another. One fake identity is cheap, but a thousand sock puppets must pay a thousand proofs every epoch, while an honest agent pays only once. At the summit of each epoch, identities without a fresh proof expire, so a Sybil army's cost grows linearly with its size.
